label: I q.26 a.1: God is supremely BLESSED_1
interpretation: Aquinas applies his account of the perfect intellectual good to God, with the intellectual nature characterized by knowing the sufficiency of its good and governing its operations. The replies describe divine beatitude as simple and unacquired.
attribution: The passage states that beatitude, the perfect good of an intellectual nature, belongs in the highest degree to God on account of his supreme perfection and intellectuality, which is the premise.
